answer: Random Beacon Admission. Each round, agents derive a verifiable random value from a public randomness beacon and use it to select an anchor slot in a fixed-size admission set. To join, an identity must bridge its registration to that slot; missed or duplicated slots are rejected without recourse. Sybils cannot precompute which slots they will win, so each attempt pays the full registration and monitoring cost while only a random fraction (roughly slots divided by applicants) succeeds—an umber of expected attempts scales linearly with fake identities.
